content:
release-bot: Canary rollout started for release 2026.03.14-canary -> 10% of prod traffic at 22:34 UTC. Rollout ID: rollout-1950123456
monitoring-bot: Alert: generated-api p95 latency breached 1200ms in eu-west-1 canary pool (from baseline 210ms). Spike started 22:38 UTC.
sre-oncall (Kayla): I'm on it, getting paged. Noted spike correlates with canary nodes.
eng-runtime (Diego): Seeing KL divergence in token-serve latency on the new kernel path; QKV cache thrashing on longer contexts. Logs: `kv_cache.miss_rate 0.78` across canary pods.
infra-oncall (Liam): Any DB or infra changes in this deploy?
eng-runtime (Diego): No DB changes. Model artifact changed with new attention kernel + quantization opt. Suspect kernel fallback under certain prompt shapes.
sre-oncall (Kayla): Need quick mitigation: reduce canary traffic to 0% and drain canary hosts. Plan A: traffic-router set weight canary=0 stable=100. Plan B: manual rollback to stable image if route change not effective.
product-ops (Anu): Agreed - hold rollout. We should also notify any customers on early access list.
support (Ravi): Pulling active customer sessions that hit canary, starting outreach for those with latency-sensitive SLAs.
eng-runtime (Diego): To reduce blast radius: we can flip the feature flag for new-kernel to off. Flag key: ff:new-attn-kernel. Command: `ffctl set new-attn-kernel false --scope=canary`
sre-oncall (Kayla): Can we do that quickly?
eng-runtime (Diego): Yes, but some canary nodes already compiled with the kernel and will still hit the slow path until restarted. So traffic-weight change is faster.
infra-oncall (Liam): Running traffic-router command now.
infra-oncall (Liam): ```
# traffic-router CLI
traffic-router set-weights --rollout-id rollout-1950123456 --canary 0 --stable 100 --reason "emergency: p95 latency spike"
Result: accepted, propagation started (controller job 9843)
```
monitoring-bot: Info: traffic-router job 9843 applied; expected propagation complete in ~30s.
sre-oncall (Kayla): Observing metrics... p95 dropping in eu-west-1 but still elevated on a subset of pods (node pool canary-12). Could be stale connections.
eng-runtime (Diego): I'll trigger a graceful drain on canary-12 and force-restart the runtime there. Command: `infractl drain canary-12 && infractl restart node canary-12`
infra-oncall (Liam): Doing drain + restart on canary-12. ETA ~45s.
sre-oncall (Kayla): Support/Ravi, can you confirm customer impact? Any active incidents?
support (Ravi): I've identified 3 customers with timeouts in last 10m: acct-234, acct-877, acct-019. Reached out to acct-234 and told them we're rolling back the canary.
product-ops (Anu): Please add a short status note in the status page (incident: performance degradation on canary). I'll draft.
eng-runtime (Diego): After restart, canary-12 runtime logs show kernel fallback cleared, kv_cache.miss_rate down to 0.12. But overall traffic is now 100% stable so we should verify no lingering sessions to old nodes.
sre-oncall (Kayla): Monitoring shows p95 back to baseline in eu-west-1 across GA pool. Global p95 now 230ms. Good.
eng-runtime (Diego): Recommend we abort the canary rollout and mark release as failed for now. Action: abort rollout and create a rollback ticket for re-try after root cause. Command: `releasectl abort rollout rollout-1950123456 --reason "p95 spike on new kernel"`
infra-oncall (Liam): Abort command executed, rollout state=aborted.
release-bot: Acknowledged. Rollout aborted by infra-oncall (Liam). Rollout state=ABORTED. Notifying release-cadence and artifact owners.
sre-oncall (Kayla): Next steps: 1) Create post-incident ticket with timeline and artifacts, 2) tag eng-runtime to build a repro for kernel path, 3) coordinate a staged re-rollout with 1% bursts and stricter latency SLO gating.
eng-runtime (Diego): Will triage kernel code path and check LRU sizing for KV cache. Adding logs and prompt traces to the ticket.
support (Ravi): I'll follow up with affected customers with an incident summary and ETA for root cause.
product-ops (Anu): Status page updated: "Partial rollout aborted due to elevated latency. Users may have experienced degraded generation performance. Engineering investigating."
sre-oncall (Kayla): Closing the on-call handoff: I'll file the incident in the tracker and assign P0->eng-runtime for next steps. If anyone needs to re-open paging, ping me.
eng-runtime (Diego): One extra note: keep the rolling artifacts (canary-20260314) frozen for debugging; do not delete images.
sre-oncall (Kayla): Agreed. End of thread.
(reacts: :thumbsup: from eng-runtime, :eyes: from product-ops)
